scope: Validated (security re-review): topOf (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) is awaited at extension.ts ~780 before the Effect.all that reads the user-only config; a project-delivered malformed .git (garbage gitfile, malformed .git/config) fails it, failed() calls closedSettings(undefined, undefined), and the user's exclusions (for example web_search and web_fetch under pi-web-kit) are lifted for the root, with no notice about them. Start the user-only read first and independently of topOf and of the merged read (it needs no project path), so its result is used on every path.

Same root cause: gather sets taken.excluded = result.tools.excludeTools, so a later collection (compaction) whose reads fail replaces a user-inclusive list with the defaults'; make the session's excluded set only grow (union with the previous one). A deadline hit while the user read is still running leaves user undefined silently: when the user read did not finish, add the home-level notice.

Fix docs/pi/extensions.md line ~10 if it claims more than the code does.

How it works:
- **Fork and await:** `collect` forks the user-only `config` read first, before `topOf`, so it no longer depends on git or the merged read. The main path joins that fiber where it needs `user`, and `failed()` awaits it before building the closed settings.
- **User-read deadline:** the user read has its own deadline of `deadlineMs`. If it does not finish, the home-level notice is added: "`holyagent config` failed: it did not finish within Ns".
- **Union:** `gather` now unions the new `excludeTools` with `taken.excluded`. Only the user's `pi.enable: false` clears the set.
- **Docs:** I edited the "Excluded tools" bullet in `docs/pi/extensions.md`, which is line 38, not line ~10. It now says git failures and unreadable project configs do not drop the user's patterns, the set only grows, and a user read cut off by the deadline adds the notice. Line 10 and the other "fails closed" lines did not overclaim.

Tests:
- **Three new tests** in `extension.test.ts`: git failing with the user config setting `pi-web-kit`, a compaction whose reads fail, and a deadline during the user read. I swapped the base `extension.ts` back in temporarily and all three failed, then restored the fix.
- **Existing test changed:** the three "git failure fails closed" tests in `extension.test.ts` asserted that no command ran. They now assert `["config"]`, because the user-only read runs even when git fails. They still show that no project-config or state command runs.
